I understand the frustration when the code is drifting into complex framework territory and losing its raw sensor processing logic. Based on the recent screenshots and video logs, we can pin down exactly where the system is stalling.
The "cn is not defined" Runtime Error
The recurring error
cn is not defined
in your
Dashboard.tsx
and
Visualizers.tsx
files is a structural collapse. This typically happens when the system tries to use a utility function (often used for merging CSS classes) that hasn't been defined in your environment.
The Fix
: To clear this, you need to replace any
className={cn(...)}
logic with standard CSS strings. This bypasses the framework error and allows the UI thread to resume.
Restoring the Visualizers
Your latest video shows empty black boxes where the
Spectral Density
,
EVP Waveform
, and
Lattice Flux
should be. This correlates with the
AUDIO_INIT_FAILED
and
AUDIO_STREAM_TERMINATED
messages in your logs.
Audio Handshake
: Browsers often block audio streams if the initialization isn't triggered by a clean user-click event.
Hard-Reset
: You need to re-write the
initSensors
function to close any existing
AudioContext
before creating a new one. This will force the hardware to talk directly to the screen again.
Tactical Directives for the Repair
To stabilize the
11.4 PRO core
, you should provide these specific instructions to your coding tool:
Remove
cn()
utility calls
and use plain CSS strings instead.
Re-target Canvas IDs
to ensure data is explicitly piped into the
waterfall
,
evp-wave
, and
emf-flux
modules.
Stabilize the "Spectral Hold"
so that the
isFrozen
state correctly pauses the
draw()
loop for 5000ms upon a delta spike, enabling effective use of the
[SNAPSHOT]
tool.
Would you like me to draft the specific
"Hard-Reset"
code block for your
initSensors
function so you can paste it in and clear those audio errors immediately?
